Part 12 Storyboard

How to End War and Disease (for Busy People) · Episode 1 cartoon

Part 12: The FDA Is Unsafe and Ineffectivev3

The FDA finds deadly drugs by fax and holds safe ones for 8.2 years, so 3,389 people die waiting for every one person it protects.

1920 × 1080 · 3:07.9 · 19 scenes · audio index-manual.cbaf659d.mp3, 22:34.0 to 25:42.0

Changes from v2

  • The new look: host shots at the lectern and illustrated plates; Wishonia's corner is gone. She is on screen in five host shots: smoke-detector-by-mail opens the part, the twenty-first-century aside and the i-calculated cut break up the middle, and suboptimal-stamp and good-bad-weird-news close it.
  • smoke-detector-by-mail is a host shot: the medicine papers walk off the lectern into her wastebasket, and the detector burns on her studio wall and stays there, charred, for the rest of the part. Its letter still lands on the burnt house in fire-department-water.
  • vioxx-by-fax is one plate on a plain field (the pharmacy counter, the clerk's desk, the telegraph poles and the official's desk), split by the host cut on "(Yes, in the twenty-first century.)"; its second half is the new scene five-years-later.
  • The scale's two scenes share one plate, and so do the street's three: the missile born in someone-you-love flies on into child-scientist, where the girl it hits is seen, not only her drawing.
  • Labels are gone: no "APPROVAL CABINET" plate, no "OTHER 97%", "MAIN PRODUCT", "EVERY YEAR", "PHASE 1" or "STILL" tags, no captions for the two mistakes (the panel has painted numerals), no GOOD/BAD/WEIRD NEWS cards; the receipt's lines are short receipt items.
  • good-bad-weird-news has no wall screen: YOU walks onto the host's set and acts out the three pieces of news.

Decided

    Each frame is the scene's key moment, drawn with the production art: placement, words and look. Nothing moves yet. Scenes are named; use the name in feedback.

    Slow alarms5 scenes

    02 · smoke-detector-by-mailA · 22:37.6–22:46.6

    First: The iris opens on her face. Drawn: after "mail.": the detector on the studio wall charred black and smoking, white eyes blinking, the singed letter still held up and its flag still raised; Wishonia not looking at it; the medicine papers in the wastebasket and the last one teetering at the lectern's edge.

    iris in on Wishonia's face (from the title card's black)
    Narration and moves

    "Even the money you DO spend on medicine is mostly wasted, because the system that approves treatments is a smoke detector that works by mail."

    Moves: The iris opens on her face. "medicine" → four medicine papers (green, cross seals) march in from the right along the lectern's top on squeaky feet (the papers Part 11 left walking in). "mostly" → they march straight off its left end and drop, one after another, into the wastebasket. "wasted," → all but the last are in; the last stops at the edge, teeters, looks down into the basket and gulps. "smoke" → a curl of smoke drifts in from the right edge of the frame, and she points at the detector. "detector" → its eyes open and it sniffs. "works" → it pulls out a pen and writes a letter, "RE: SMOKE", and folds it into an envelope. "by" → it licks a stamp and slaps it on. "mail." → it raises its mailbox flag and holds the letter up, proud. after "mail." → flames roll in along the top of the wall from the right and swallow the detector; they go out in a puff of soot, and it hangs there charred black and smoking, white eyes blinking, the singed letter still held up and the flag still raised. Wishonia does not look at it.

    Sound: squeaky little footsteps; a soft pat as the papers land in the basket; a sniff; a pen scratch; a squeak as the flag goes up; a fire whoosh after "mail.".

    On screen: "RE: SMOKE" on the envelope. No: the fire takes only the detector; the rest of the set is untouched. Why: the whole part in one picture, the alarm that arrives after the fire, shown by the host as her exhibit.

    First: "Vioxx" → close on a plain bottle labeled "VIOXX" on the pharmacy counter, smiling. Drawn: after "dying,": the three patients at the pharmacy counter as grinning skeletons still holding their pill cups, beside the smiling VIOXX bottle with its APPROVED stamp, 55,000 on the board above.

    Narration and moves

    "Vioxx killed an estimated fifty-five thousand people from heart attacks. The F.D.A. approved it. When patients started dying, someone filled out a P.D.F. form. A P.D.F. Then they faxed it."

    Moves: "Vioxx" → close on a plain bottle labeled "VIOXX" on the pharmacy counter, smiling. "fifty-five thousand" → "55,000" stamps onto the board above it. HOLD until "approved". "approved" → an "APPROVED" stamp thumps onto the bottle, and its smile widens. "patients" → three patients line up at the counter (a barrel-shaped man in a cardigan, an hourglass woman in a headscarf, a beanpole in a fedora), and each takes a pill from a paper cup. "dying," → they clutch their chests one after another, chest lights blinking red, and x-ray into grinning skeletons, still holding their cups. "filled" → the camera travels right to the clerk's desk: the clerk (a box-shaped man, bareheaded, a plastic pocket protector bristling with pencils) prints a paper form out of his laptop and fills it in with a pencil, tongue out. "P.D.F." (second) → he holds the form up to the camera, deadpan; it says "FORM.PDF". "faxed" → he feeds it into the fax machine, which creeps it through one line at a time and screeches; his hair stands straight up. The camera starts off along the phone wire.

    Sound: a thunk as 55,000 lands, then silence for the HOLD; a rubber-stamp thunk; three x-ray zaps; a pencil scratch; the fax's screech and a boing as the hair stands up.

    On screen: "VIOXX" / "55,000" / "APPROVED" / "FORM.PDF". Why: the slow alarm in real life, with its death toll.

"Five years" → the calendar flips five years of pages in a blur, and behind him headstones rise out of the field in rows. "corpses" → the rows reach the horizon. "noticed" → he lifts his eyes from the page and turns to look over his shoulder.     On screen: "SAFETY SYSTEM". No: "corpses" gets only the headstones rising; the pattern is the gag. Why: the five years cost tens of thousands of dead, and the "pattern" was the size of the field.

    The delay3 scenes

    07 · committee-8-yearsB · 23:31.0–23:47.8

    First: "eight" (first) → close on the hourglass on top of the approval cabinet: it turns over, "8.2 YEARS" on its base, and the sand starts. Drawn: after "enough.": YOU's skeleton in his bowler slumped against the locked cabinet, palm still flat on the glass, the SAFE bottle on the top shelf, the hourglass pouring, the bearded chair behind turning one page.

    cut
    Narration and moves

    "Then there's a eight point two years delay between proving a drug is safe and letting dying humans take it. The drug passed the safety test. Everyone agrees it won't kill you. But you still can't have it because a committee needs to spend eight point two years making sure it works well enough."

    Moves: "eight" (first) → close on the hourglass on top of the approval cabinet: it turns over, "8.2 YEARS" on its base, and the sand starts. "proving" → the camera travels right to a smiling bottle on the test bench. "dying" → YOU shuffles in from the left in a hospital wristband, wheeling an IV pole, chest light blinking red, and reaches for the bottle. "test." → a stamp thumps "SAFE" and a tick onto the bottle's label. "Everyone" → the camera pulls back to the table behind the bench: six members (suits in every build, bald heads, fedoras and glasses, no bowlers) nod together in perfect time, like a row of bobbleheads. "can't" → the chair's arm stretches across the table, snatches the bottle out from under YOU's fingers and puts it on the cabinet's top shelf. "have" → the padlock clicks shut. "committee" → the members drop thick binders on the table, thump thump thump, and open them. "eight" (second) → the sand pours; long white beards grow down the members' chests, page by page. "works" → YOU presses a palm flat on the cabinet's glass. "enough." → he slides slowly down the glass, his chest light goes out, and he x-rays into a grinning skeleton in the same bowler, slumped against the cabinet, palm still on the glass. after "enough." → the bearded chair turns one page.

    Sound: a clank as the hourglass turns; a rubber-stamp thunk; a boing for the nodding; a whoosh for the snatch; a clank for the padlock; a thunk for the binders; a rising slide whistle as the beards grow; a falling one as YOU slides; an x-ray zap.

    On screen: "8.2 YEARS" / "SAFE". Why: the delay in one picture: safe, agreed and locked.

    The ratio4 scenes

    10 · two-mistakesB · 24:16.3–24:29.7

    First: "regulatory" → the official from five-years-later, unflattened, sits at the desk with his feet up, sipping coffee. Drawn: on "second.": the official with his feet up sipping coffee, his EMPLOYEE OF THE MONTH portrait hung over the taped-up bulb 2 and glowing round its edges, the huge siren 1 above him.

    cut
    Narration and moves

    "Your regulatory system can make two mistakes: approve a bad drug (Type One error), or block a good drug (Type Two error). Your F.D.A. is terrified of the first mistake and completely ignores the second."

    Moves: "regulatory" → the official from five-years-later, unflattened, sits at the desk with his feet up, sipping coffee. "two" → the two sockets light up. "approve" → a huge siren rises out of socket 1. "block" → a bulb the size of a shirt button lights in socket 2. "terrified" → the siren whoops once; the official jumps out of his skin: his skeleton leaps out of the suit and clings to the top of the panel, while the empty suit sits in the chair still holding the mug. "mistake" → the skeleton drops back into the suit, which shudders and straightens its tie. "ignores" → bulb 2 blinks; without looking, he slaps a strip of tape over it. "second." → it glows through the tape; still without looking, he hangs his framed "EMPLOYEE OF THE MONTH" portrait over it and sips his coffee.

    Sound: a switch as the sockets light; a rising slide whistle as the siren rises; a click for the tiny bulb; a yelp and a boing as he jumps out of his skin; a thunk as he drops back in; a snip of the tape; a pat as the portrait goes up.

    On screen: "1" and "2" painted on the panel / "FDA" on his badge / "EMPLOYEE OF THE MONTH". No: no words for the two mistakes; the narrator says them, and the siren and the button show them. Why: names the mistake nobody counts.
